source.title: Disentangling MLP Neuron Weights in Vocabulary Space
source.authors: Asaf Avrahamy; Yoav Gur-Arieh; Mor Geva

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether channel descriptions explain neuron activations, using generated activating/neutral examples and a matching task rather than the original pole-share audit.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs, Qwen3, vision-model estimates, attribution graphs, or activation-simulator scores. Its input-side faithfulness and completeness evaluations bear on V6, but they use descriptions of ROTATE channels (and SAE features), not explanations based only on activating examples. The reported channel ablations are recorded as findings outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It introduces ROTATE, a data-free rotation of neuron weights into vocabulary channels. It reports how well its own channel descriptions perform (faithfulness, completeness, head-to-head win rates) against SAE and activation-based baselines. It never reports how many of a model's neurons have one main job. It never scores how well a neuron's activating-example explanation predicts where the neuron fires. The input-side scores are channel-description pass rates under the study's own pipeline, so they measure the method's quality rather than any version's effect. Polysemanticity is assumed in the motivation, not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that ROTATE recovers faithful, causally separable vocabulary channels from weights alone, beating SAE baselines on faithfulness and completeness. They also find that aggregated channel descriptions beat activation-based neuron descriptions by 2–3× in head-to-head win rates. They note limits: vocabulary-orthogonal functions are out of scope, and only two layers in each of two models were evaluated.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a data-free weight-space rotation and kurtosis method, then evaluates channel descriptions using generated examples and LLM matching; it does not reproduce the cited neuron-explainer audit or measure pole-level job shares.
record.method_sensitivity: Scores differ across layers and models; the authors report strongest gains in middle-to-late layers and weaker faithfulness in Gemma layer 4.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating an output vocabulary channel cuts its decoded tokens by 87–90%; ablating another channel raises them by 14–24%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-derived vocabulary channels separately control distinct parts of a neuron's output.

fits_no_version.finding: Fig. 4 (no rows): in Llama-3.1-8B, ROTATE channel descriptions beat simulator-optimised top-activation descriptions (MaxAct++) in 63–69% of comparisons on activation ranks 100–500. The authors say activation-based methods have limited coverage beyond peak behaviour. This is relative judge preference only, with no rate of explained firing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron descriptions built from top-activating examples cover moderate activations worse than weight-derived descriptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-side ablation of a neuron's top channel drives its activation toward 0, while other channels leave it near 1 (Fig. 3; no rows).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gate-weight vocabulary channels are causally responsible for separate subsets of a neuron's firing.

record.problems: The study evaluates only two selected layers per model in its main setup and uses LLM-generated examples and LLM judges for key evaluations; its own limitation section notes that vocabulary-orthogonal functions are outside scope and that additional scales and architectures remain to be tested.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B pole audit or shares of one-job, two-job and unexplained poles.
No shares of interpretable neurons in any model. Appendix B plots vocabulary kurtosis across families, but that is a different construct.
No InceptionV1 or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No share of interpretable neurons by tool or architecture, and no test of the proposed causes of messy neurons. Tool comparisons rank description methods only.
No attribution graphs or circuits; circuit use is mentioned only as future work.
No score of whether an activating-example explanation of a neuron predicts where it fires on held-out text. Faithfulness tests ROTATE channel descriptions; head-to-head gives only relative win rates.
No simulator correlation scores reported; MaxAct++ simulator-optimised descriptions appear only as a pairwise baseline.

missing.what: Llama-3.1-8B layer 4 (49.7 / 41.3) and layer 8 (49.3 / 35.8) faithfulness and completeness; T45/T46 wrongly record dashes. Not version-relevant.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V6 links is not supported. Every input-side number scores the study's own channel descriptions or the SAE/random baselines. These are method comparisons and say nothing about how much of a neuron an activating-example explanation captures. The study assumes neurons are mostly polysemantic, which runs against V1's premise, but it does not measure this. Rows T33–T50 partly duplicate Table 1.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or proportions of poles with one, two, or unknown jobs.
No cross-model or scale audit of shares of poles with one or more jobs; the models and layers studied do not establish such shares.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.

The study compares tools on channel faithfulness and completeness, but does not estimate the share of interpretable neurons across tools or architectures, test the proposed causes of messy neurons, or study InceptionV1-sized vision models.
No attribution graphs or test of explaining model behaviour without a replacement model and its reconstruction error.

Tests channel descriptions with synthetic activating/neutral examples and an LLM matching task; it does not test explanations based only on activating examples against held-out natural firing locations.
No scoring by simulating explanation-predicted activations on new text, or comparison of explainer-model strength for that score.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ROTATE input-side descriptions in the tested layers and models
reader_labels.reason: Faithfulness scores are 0.46–0.71 and completeness scores are 0.49–0.60 in the main evaluation, showing incomplete description-to-activation correspondence; see T1–T8. The layer sweep also reports non-perfect scores across evaluated layers; see T33–T50.
